extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to Nature Sustainability and other Nature Portfolio journals; institutional press officers; journalists covering Nature Portfolio content
extracted.subtask_description: Policies governing interaction with the media for submissions and accepted papers to Nature Portfolio journals: when and how authors and journalists may publicize work, embargo timing, preprint/conference rules, and enforcement. Covers advance access for journalists and coordination with press offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of media coverage by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid contacting journalists to solicit coverage of submitted manuscripts. For permitted communications see the 'Timing for author-media discussion' criterion and the 'Communication between scientists' section regarding preprints and conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for author–media discussion for accepted contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may speak to media in the narrow window (up to one week before publication) but must strictly observe the embargo time and date stated on the press release. Coordinate with the journal press office when planning publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release distribution and advance access for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce and distribute press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists. Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover, and are given the names and contact details of corresponding authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material (for example, an accompanying News and Views article, and any extra images provided by the authors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo on press releases and papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties (authors, institutional press offices, journalists) must not publish or publicize embargoed material before the stated time/date. The embargo exists to provide fair and equal access and allow journalists to base coverage on the complete, final paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial highlighting of especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a paper is highlighted, authors may receive calls or emails from the media; they are encouraged to cooperate with journalists so that media coverage of their work is accurate and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors arranging their own publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If arranging independent publicity, authors should synchronize timing and messaging with the journal's press office to avoid breaching embargoes or producing conflicting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for embargoes and peer review benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nature Portfolio journals believe that their media embargo serves scientists, authors, journalists and the public. Our policy is to release information about our content in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing it to provide informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper that is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes allow journalists to obtain informed reactions from independent researchers and to have confidence stemming from peer review; premature release denies journalists that confidence and impairs informed coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for journalists who break embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list, and we shall continue to use this sanction when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking an embargo can result in exclusion from future advance-access distributions; journals will enforce embargoes by removing offending journalists from circulation lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations do not constitute prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals do not wish to hinder communication among researchers. We support open communications between researchers whether on a recognised community preprint server or preprint commenting platforms, through discussions at research meetings or online collaborative sites such as wikis or the author's blog. Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may display drafts of their research papers on an established preprint server before or during submission to Nature or any Nature journal. Exposure of preprints on servers does not preempt their submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to media about preprints or conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation, by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context. In these circumstances, media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approached by reporters about a preprint, researchers should make it clear the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that the findings are provisional and that the conclusions may change. Be aware such coverage may reduce or pre-empt coverage by other media at the time of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of peer review and editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to keep the details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose peer review exchanges or confidential editorial deliberations when communicating with journalists or the public; maintain confidentiality even if discussing preprints or earlier versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal recommends explicit labelling and caution in reporting on preprints to inform audiences about the provisional status of findings.
